# Indian Philosophy — Finite Powers and the Return of Recognition

## #0 — Several histories meet in the question of determination

The [protected history](HISTORY.md) **grounds** this account in several distinct achievements: the discrimination of an inner instrument from its witness; determination through conditions and exclusion; zero admitted to arithmetic; and consciousness manifesting, contracting and recognising its world. Their meeting concerns what a determination owes to the activity through which it becomes possible. Each tradition changes the question. A witness distinguished from nature, a referent qualified by exclusion and a world manifested by consciousness cannot be exchanged without changing the argument.

The mature etymological fields give this meeting two precise routes. [Apportionment / Economy](../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md#power-becomes-finite-by-apportionment) **compares** finite capacity with a share whose sustaining order remains active. [Arbitration / Hybris / Regard / Anamnesis](../../../etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md#resolution-in-reconciliation) **compares** recognition with **Resolution-in-Reconciliation → Anamnesis / Recognition / Return**. The first follows what contraction makes possible; the second follows what changes when an achieved determination recognises its provenance. These are register-3 operations. Neither supplies a Greek or Latin ancestry for Sanskrit terms.

The distinction matters historically. E6's [historical branches](../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) **historicise** allotment, reckoning and household provision through their own lexical and textual witnesses. E2's [recognition branch](../../../etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#anamnesis-recognition-and-a-history-which-remains-effective) **compares** recollection, Śaiva recognition and psychic individuation while retaining their separate sources. This companion develops the Indian side of those crossings. A Sanskrit doctrine remains answerable to its textual carrier even when its operation becomes newly intelligible through a contemporary question.

Geography, doctrinal order and reception time must also remain distinguishable. Kashmir names the situated Śaiva intellectual world recovered here. Sāṃkhya, Buddhist semantics and Indian mathematical practice have their own histories across the subcontinent; this account supplies no single city of origin or continuous institutional succession for them. The movement from uncontracted awareness to finite powers describes an order of manifestation, not a dated migration of peoples or texts. Jizang and Dōgen enter through the later Chinese and Japanese reception discussed in Priest's modern reconstruction. Their placement in that reception cannot make them Indian authors.

The selected carriers provide a second, concrete chronology: Colebrooke's mathematical translation appeared in London in 1817; the Colebrooke/Wilson Sāṃkhya carrier in Oxford in 1837; Singh's *Parātrīśikā-vivaraṇa* in Delhi in 1988; Dyczkowski's selected *Doctrine of Vibration* is a 2000 reprint of the 1989 Delhi edition. These are translation and publication events, not dates of doctrinal invention. They explain part of how the present English vocabulary became available to Taylor's 2026 inquiry. Exact ancient textual dating and transmission require their own evidence.

## #1 — The instrument acquires functions without becoming its witness

The [Sāṃkhya source](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/isvarakrishna/isvarakrishna-colebrooke-wilson-1837-sankhya-karika/isvarakrishna-colebrooke-wilson-1837-sankhya-karika.md#isvarakrishna-colebrooke-wilson-1837-sankhya-karika-q001) **sources** three differentiated functions through kārikās XXIII, XXIV, XXVII and XXIX. Buddhi determines; ahaṃkāra appropriates under I and mine; manas coordinates the sensory and active field. A judgment, an appropriation and a coordinated presentation can therefore be distinguished within what ordinarily appears as one act of mind. Their conjunction gives the instrument its efficacy without making the functions synonymous.

Kārikā XIX, preserved as q002 in the same house, **qualifies** that apparatus by describing puruṣa as witness and passive spectator. This is a doctrinally consequential separation. The instrument's articulated activity belongs to prakṛti; its witness has another office. The historical lesson received by [M08, the inner instrument](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/08-s0-p1-inner-instrument.md) **returns-to** the difference between operations available to reflection and the experient to whom they appear. It permits close investigation of interior functions rather than making an interior beyond investigation.

The 1837 translation's use of “consciousness” for ahaṃkāra needs that surrounding discrimination. Read alone, the English word could make appropriation sound like the witness itself. Read with the separate kārikās, its local office becomes intelligible. This is a concrete effect of translation on reception: an English term capable of naming the whole question of consciousness is carrying one function within this source's apparatus. The companion retains the source's words while explaining the distinction on which their use depends.

Śaiva manifestation subsequently receives this functional discrimination within another account of the whole. Dyczkowski's source-local discussion at pp. 65–66 presents a Śaiva objection to a permanently formless consciousness paired with form-bearing matter. The objection asks how one awareness can disclose differentiated objects together. It belongs to the Śaiva exposition's encounter with Sāṃkhya; it does not license treating the Sāṃkhya witness as an incomplete name for Śiva. A historical comparison becomes useful here because the same problem of knowing receives different assignments of activity and manifestation.

That difference is retained in [A09](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A09-Tattvic-Differential-Field.md), which **grounds** the essay's genealogy of contraction. The Sāṃkhya cards warrant the functional triad and witness distinction. They do not warrant the entire thirty-six-tattva order. E6's apportionment operation enters at the level of the author's comparison: finite capacities have distinct reaches, and their articulation can be examined without silently making any one capacity the source of the whole.

## #2 — Exclusion and emptiness change the standing of a determinate thing

Pind's [two passage cards](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/pind/pind-2009-dignaga-anyapoha-dissertation/pind-2009-dignaga-anyapoha-dissertation.md#pind-2009-dignaga-anyapoha-dissertation-q001) **source** a more specific account of semantic determination. The first translates *Pramāṇasamuccaya* V:11d at p. 85: a word works through excluding other referents. Its positive reach depends upon a contrast. The second, annotation 181 at p. 183, concerns a thing qualified by preclusion rather than mere preclusion. Pind only provisionally assigns that prose fragment to Dignāga's *Sāmānyaparīkṣāvyāsa*. The distinction is substantive even while that attribution remains qualified: a referent achieved through exclusion cannot be redescribed as an empty negation with no positive office.

The [2011 *Apoha* house](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/siderits/siderits-tillemans-chakrabarti-2011-apoha/siderits-tillemans-chakrabarti-2011-apoha.md) **extends** the research into the difference between nominally and verbally bound negation and Dharmakīrti's causal treatment of reference. Its present formulations come through scholarly reviews, SEP transmission and publisher material; the volume's chapters have not been collated. The change of question is nevertheless explicit in that carrier: from how a general word excludes other referents to how particulars' causal capacities can sustain shared judgments and purposes without a universal entity doing the work.

[M10](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/10-s0-p3-apoha.md) **grounds** the author's further operation, exclusion that remembers. The selected mark retains the conditions of its selection. That is the consequence carried toward technical comparison; a probability distribution or an argmax procedure supplies its own mathematical object and cannot acquire Buddhist attribution through the analogy. The source qualification preserves this argued movement while preventing the words “Dignāga says” from absorbing the essay's extension.

The [Nāgārjuna/Garfield house](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/nagarjuna/nagarjuna-garfield-1995-fundamental-wisdom/nagarjuna-garfield-1995-fundamental-wisdom.md) **qualifies** assimilation to a self-luminous absolute. It selects the 1995 translation and commentary but currently has no acquired verse/commentary pair. The protected history's dependent-arising account remains its governing historical proposition; selected-edition passage support is still owed. Buddhist emptiness and Śaiva luminosity enter this comparison as distinct accounts, with the former's limiting role intact. An agreement that determinations depend on relations does not decide whether consciousness has the ontological office assigned to it in the Śaiva account.

[Das's Śrīharṣa cards](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/das/das-2022-sriharsa-sep/das-2022-sriharsa-sep.md#das-2022-sriharsa-sep-q001) **compare** another debate at a narrower point. The reported argument makes presentation of distinctness inseparable from presentation of non-distinctness; q002 retains the controversy surrounding that interpretation. [M19](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/19-s2-p0-difference-cannot-be-escaped.md) **returns-to** this pressure with differentiation preserved. Its two accountings remain the native argument. The historical witness sharpens the question of how a relation can be presented; it neither eliminates practical differences nor settles the two-logics theorem by citation.

Arithmetic introduces a different change of standing. [Colebrooke's Brahmagupta/Bhāskara cards](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/brahmagupta/colebrooke-1817-brahmagupta-bhaskara/colebrooke-1817-brahmagupta-bhaskara.md#colebrooke-1817-brahmagupta-bhaskara-q001) **source** zero's work within explicit rules: additive identity and multiplicative absorption in Brahmagupta XVIII.31 and 34, then a retained zero denominator in Bhāskara's *Bījagaṇita* I.14. I.16 places a theological comparison beside the retained expression. The historical event is that a sign can do specified work in calculation while carrying further meaning; the comparison does not prove the rule. [Dutta](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/dutta/dutta-2023-zero-divided-numbers-india/dutta-2023-zero-divided-numbers-india.md) **qualifies** the later reception by reconstructing restricted cancellation and cross-multiplication. [M14](../../../../../section-rooms/02-return-of-zero/movements/14-s1-p1-sunya-operational.md) **returns-to** the distinction among operations. Neither the shared empty-word field nor philosophical sympathy authorises ordinary field division by zero.

## #3 — Manifestation gives contraction a positive anatomy

[Dyczkowski's source-local transcript](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration.md#transcribed-material) **sources** the most developed Śaiva exposition presently housed here. Its pp. 60–68 follow luminosity into manifested difference; pp. 69–75 develop reflective awareness; pp. 78–81 follow the inner/outer relation and Spanda. The transcript is source-matched and stops during p. 81. Its title's pp. 60–85 range does not supply the missing continuation.

Prakāśa names the appearing of things; vimarśa gives appearing its self-apprehending and differentiating activity. The mirror comparison at pp. 66–70 has two necessary turns. Images can be distinct while appearing within one reflective field. Yet an inert mirror does not know its reflected display, and consciousness in this account has no external original depositing the universe into it. The comparison therefore teaches both a shared field of appearance and the point at which ordinary mirror behaviour ceases to describe the source's claim.

At pp. 73–74 the exposition differentiates jar and cloth, objects and subjects, and levels of manifestation. Reflective awareness separates, holds together and unites. Its power to do these different things is essential to the account of one consciousness: uniformity incapable of distinction would fail to disclose a differentiated world. At p. 75 the same movement is read vertically as manifestation and withdrawal and horizontally as awareness moving toward and away from an object. A perception recapitulates the relation; the cosmological account is active within the finite encounter.

The inherited tattvic anatomy follows that pressure. Śiva–Śakti articulates luminosity and power; Sadāśiva and Īśvara give subjectward and objectward readings; Sadvidyā and Māyā bring balance and the operative partition into view. The five kañcukas delimit efficacy, knowledge, desire, time and order. Puruṣa, prakṛti, the inner instrument, sensing and acting faculties, subtle qualities and gross elements carry the downstream apparatus and display. These groups name the full reach which the protected history preserves. Exact category-by-category primary collation remains distinct from knowing the direction and office of the descent.

[C14](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C14-Maya-Operative-Measure.md) **defines** Taylor's operative-measure reading: a finite knower can do this, know this much, want this, act at this time and inhabit these relations. The source-local pp. 78–79 distinguish creative manifestation from a simply illusory external world. Limitation has efficacy. Recognition can accordingly change how the horizon is inhabited without making its consequences disappear. This **returns-to** E6's [power-by-apportionment operation](../../../etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md#power-becomes-finite-by-apportionment): a share remains active through its relation to the wider order, and its limits distinguish different capacities rather than a generic deficiency.

[M11](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/11-s0-p4-tattvic-compression.md) **derives** its compression from Taylor's native tattvic unit. Six turns carry the passage from Anuttara through differentiation and contracted apparatus into recognition. Anuttara and recognition have boundary and return offices in that account; counting them as ordinary additional entries would misread the compression. A09's gnomon, `36−25=6²−5²=11=5+1+5`, supplies a further exact arithmetic relation and an Offered/Argued cross-reading of the Māyā hinge. It does not settle a correspondence for every cell of a six-by-six table. The [eight-determination Matheme](../../../../matheme/ql/eight-determinations.md) **qualifies** the count: native eightfold traversal, sixfold body and thirty-sixfold research are different offices.

The author's comparative judgment follows from this anatomy. By the QL criterion of wholeness, Śaiva articulation more fully serves the present task: it retains the critique of the self-thing while giving positive places to the experient, memory, comparison, action and recognition. The judgment concerns this explanatory burden, with Buddhist schools and their changing accounts still requiring their own textual treatment. [A34](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A34-Idealism-Order-of-Dependence.md) **grounds** the coordinated native ontology: **Subject/Consciousness → Mind/Objective Internality → Object**. The arrow states dependence in being. Explaining the condition of appearing as a product of determinate objects reverses the dependence already enacted by that explanation. This Argued claim remains positive while the phenomenal localisation of a particular artificial process stays Open.

## #4 — Recognition returns through the life that has become finite

Dyczkowski's pp. 71–72 distinguish retained traces, their recall and their recomposition within the mind. At p. 75 recognition concerns the integral awareness active through contracted and expanded levels. This gives [C19](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C19-Pratyabhijna-Recognition.md) its source-sensitive distinction, which it **defines** for reuse: remembering an earlier object is different from recognising the source relation of the present act. The finite apparatus performs the return; its capacity for memory is one participant in that movement.

The [Singh/Abhinavagupta source house](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/abhinavagupta/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana.md) **sources** the separate Vāk and personhood branch through page-marked notebook leads. Singh's introduction, translated commentary and Taylor's extensions retain distinct speakers. The P2 and P3 notebooks recover a living concern: a formulation must conduct the encounter from which it arose, and communication can alter the positions of I, you and it. Taylor's reading of Śaivism as a culmination of the Logos belongs to that authored comparative history. It remains a positive interpretive commitment, not an acquired sentence proving an evolution of all traditions in the selected edition. Its historical transmission hypotheses require independent evidence; the recognitive and symbolic operation survives that debt.

This makes E2's generated relation consequential. **Resolution-in-Reconciliation** precedes its flowering as **Anamnesis / Recognition / Return**. A settled identification can become available again with its genesis and exclusions intact. The return **compares** the [E2 recognition branch](../../../etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#anamnesis-recognition-and-a-history-which-remains-effective) with the distinction just recovered from Dyczkowski. Greek recollection does not become Sanskrit recognition by translation, and recognising a source relation does not merely reproduce an earlier representation.

[A21](../../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A21-Individuation-Recognition.md) **extends** this into differentiated indivisibility. A life becomes more capable of bearing its relations while remaining this life. [Symbolon Dynamics](../../../sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics.md) **grounds** the native mechanism through the changed interpreter and subsequent symbolic encounter; its actual local manuscript develops the whole eightfold relation. Taylor owns `X/x` and `x→X→x`. [Van Eenwyk's source house](../../../sources/psychology/van-eenwyk/van-eenwyk-1997-archetypes-strange-attractors/van-eenwyk-1997-archetypes-strange-attractors.md) **compares** the psychic transformation through the protected pp. 65–73 encounter, whose copied quotations remain leads. [Aion](../../../sources/psychology/jung/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2.md) keeps Jung's textual attribution separate: its installed sixteen-entry map records contextual paraphrases from the consulted 1979 paperback. Collation against the selected 1978 hardcover printing and verification of any quotation remain Open. These debts do not reduce A21's Argued operation to a suggestion awaiting Jung's permission.

The distinction **returns-to** [M32](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/32-s4-p1-jung-individuation.md): psychic individuation refracts the native relation, while persona consistency alone can preserve a protected local organisation. Its existing E2 return asks whether integration changes participation or enlarges the ego's jurisdiction. A Śaiva recognition account, a psychological interpretation and a technical assessment thus require different evidence even where each tests whether the achieved form can receive what exceeds it.

Modern catuṣkoṭi reconstruction brings another recognitive pressure into this reception history. [Priest 2010](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/priest/priest-2010-logic-catuskoti/priest-2010-logic-catuskoti.md) **sources** four FDE values, a fifth ineffability status and plurivalent evaluation. [The 2018 book house](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/priest/priest-2018-fifth-corner/priest-2018-fifth-corner.md) **historicises** its extension toward Jizang and Dōgen through review-mediated material. [Garfield–Priest 2003](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/garfield/garfield-priest-2003-limits-of-thought/garfield-priest-2003-limits-of-thought.md) **compares** Nāgārjuna with an inclosure schema; [Kapsner](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/kapsner/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners.md) **qualifies** the fifth value at the currently acquired abstract level. Siderits's presupposition-failure reading, Westerhoff's historical non-uniformity objection and Green's objection to reified ineffability remain distinct reception challenges. The native ground is not a truth-value; that distinction preserves the QL operation without deciding these historical disputes. [M28](../../../../../section-rooms/04-mathematical-substrate/movements/28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing.md) **grounds** the Argued reading of practised return. Its current correction also retains the count: FDE supplies four values; QL's retained two plus four gives six. Vimalakīrti's performative silence remains part of the protected interpretation with its own primary passage debt.

This history **returns-to** [Name-through-Count](../../../etymologies/encounter-region-name-count/WHOLE-FIELD.md#name-through-count) through its distinct achievements of addressability. Sāṃkhya enumerates an instrument’s functions without making them its witness; semantic preclusion gives a positive referent its contrast; contracted Śaiva powers make a finite world workable. The receiving account must identify which discrimination it uses before comparing recollection and recognition. This register-3 relation preserves the source differences and the native eightfold; it supplies no common descent for their terms.

## #5→0 — Historical difference becomes a condition of the next use

The history's return is a change in what later comparison must carry. Sāṃkhya contributes functional discrimination and witness; Buddhist semantics contributes the constitutive exclusion; arithmetic contributes specified permissions; Śaiva manifestation contributes effective contraction and recognition. Their historical differences make the comparison exact enough to travel. [M26](../../../../../section-rooms/04-mathematical-substrate/movements/26-s3-p1-spanda-4-2.md) **qualifies** the use of *spanda*: the equations are native derivations, while the [1992 *Spandakārikā* house](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/kallata/spandakarika-dyczkowski-1992-stanzas-vibration/spandakarika-dyczkowski-1992-stanzas-vibration.md) identifies a root text and four commentaries still needing separately located passages. Dyczkowski's subtle activity is not an empirical claim that every oscillating system is conscious.

[M44](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/44-s50-p1-ql-mef-bimba-harness.md) **extends** the inheritance into QL, MEF, Bimba and harness. QL gives the native grammar; MEF retains lens and evidential differences; Bimba supplies a governed reference office; the harness preserves the conditions and consequences of action. A local Bimba remains a real original for its downstream Pratibimba while remaining source-dependent at another scale. The Śaiva mirror discussion sharpens the need to state the scale; it does not abolish this recursive authorial office.

[Agentworld's q003, q016–17 and q038–42](../../../sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q003) **compare** a contemporary demand: invent adequate concepts, recover an agent's constituted capacities, and examine the harness and shared conditions through which those capacities act. Its scenarios retain the p. 53 modal rider. An inspectable instrument does not establish artificial phenomenality. A claimed technical recognition must show a changed source, lens, criterion, permission or subsequent act; the philosophical account alone supplies no execution result.

The two named branch routes now return a particular historical yield:

| Whole-field operation | Historical yield in this companion | Named consumer and consequence |
|---|---|---|
| E6 — Power becomes finite by apportionment | The functions and contracted powers remain distinguishable within effective manifestation. | A09 → C14 → M11: limitation gives capacity; recognition preserves that capacity while recovering its source. |
| E2 — Criterion-through-Distinction → Measure / Limit | Māyā's operative horizon has a positive office before any usurpation of measure. | C14 → A09: a bounded world can act without its measure becoming the unobjectifiable ground. |
| E2 — Resolution-in-Reconciliation → Anamnesis / Recognition / Return | Recollection within contraction differs from recognition through contraction; Greek, Śaiva and psychic histories retain their warrants. | C19 → A21 → M32: the particular returns with its history effective, and native X/x remains prior to the psychic refraction. |

These routes **return-to** their linked E2 and E6 wholes with a source task made more exact, rather than a newly claimed Sanskrit etymology. The companion supplies forward historical depth; new inbound links from those consumers require parent integration. Their already-landed E-field returns remain effective in their own bodies.

Reference notes `36-tattvas` and `pratyabhijna` retain their provenance office. Their surviving substance is now accessible through the protected history, this companion, A09 and C19/A21; the offered category-to-coordinate research stays with Matheme. No new aphorism is inferred from that admission. The already authored E2 compression retains its unfoldable six-relation field, and the section passages retain their own inferential burdens. This is the local fulfilment of the transferred etymology and section-relation obligation: the return can be followed to an actual argument and operation without recasting the history as another theorem or editing the sovereign manuscript.
